title: fix(plugin-grid): make `object-grid` `operations` the ceiling over `rowActions` (objectui#9819)
body:
Fixes #9819

`Clause-②: no` — this narrows runtime behaviour and widens no declaration surface. Measured, not inherited: the intersection only ever refuses more than the union did, so no combination refused today becomes accepted.

## The ruling

Maintainer ruling of 2026-09-18, ruling batch #162 item 1, letter A (issue comment `5729875720`, director seat summon #24, maintainer 「同意」 12:18Z). Operative clause, quoted verbatim:

> `object-grid`'s `operations` is the CEILING: the edit gate and the delete gate in `rowCrudAffordances.ts:182` / `:184` become intersections — `rowActions` can only select an action `operations` allows; `operations: { update: false }` turns row editing off whatever `rowActions` says

⚠️ The two line addresses inside that quote are the ruling's own bytes, reproduced because the quote is verbatim; they were read from `42234b1` by the triage comment. Everywhere this pull request cites those gates in its own voice it cites them by content — they are the `canEdit` and `canDelete` assignments in `resolveRowCrudAffordances`.

⭐ **Both gates are in scope**, not only the edit one the card's title names. Re-derived by symbol on today's `origin/main` rather than trusted from the line numbers: the delete gate is textually isomorphic to the edit one, so `operations: { delete: false }` failed identically. Fixing only the edit half would have left the ruled defect half-standing.

## What changed

`resolveRowCrudAffordances`, both gates, from a union of two independently declared keys to an intersection:

- **before** — `(operations.update OR rowActions names 'edit') AND onEdit AND objectCanEdit`
- **after** — `operations.update AND onEdit AND objectCanEdit`

A truthy `operations` member is now required. Falsy covers both spellings of "not allowed": an explicit `false`, and a member a PRESENT block does not name — because a present `operations` block already REPLACED the wired-callback default instead of merging under it (that replacement is decided at the call site and was already pinned; this change does not touch it).

## What an author sees change — the cost, stated plainly

This **narrows published runtime behaviour**. An author who wrote a combination that used to render a button will now not get that button.

| The view declares | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `operations: { update: false }` plus `rowActions: ['edit']` | row Edit still rendered | Edit is gone |
| `operations: { delete: false }` plus `rowActions: ['delete']` | row Delete still rendered | Delete is gone |
| `operations: { delete: true }` plus `rowActions: ['edit']` | Edit rendered | Edit is gone — an unnamed member of a present block is not an allowance |
| no `operations` block at all | both entries, from the wired callbacks | **unchanged** |
| `rowActions: ['edit']` with no `operations` block | Edit rendered | **unchanged** |

A page that today shows an Edit or Delete affordance because `rowActions` opened it while `operations` closed it will **stop** showing it. That is the ruled direction and the point of the card: a block named `operations` that cannot turn an operation off is the trap, and the author's only observable was a button they believed was gone — no error, no warning, no degraded state. ⛔ No tolerant `??` or alias fallback was added to soften the change; a fallback here would rebuild the second de-facto contract the ruling closed.

Changeset: `@object-ui/plugin-grid` **minor**, carrying the behaviour note, exactly as the ruling directs. (Per this repo's version-alignment rule, objectui's own breaking semantics ship as `minor` with the break spelled out in the body.)

## ⭐ The pin that flipped, and why the flip is the ruling landing rather than a regression

**`packages/plugin-grid/src/__tests__/gridOperationsMembers-8071.test.tsx`** — the `object-grid.operations` member pin added by PR objectui#9817 (slice 12). Its fact 3 pinned the **union** in so many words: "They are a UNION with `rowActions`' canonical names, never an intersection — `operations: { update: false }` cannot close what `rowActions: ['edit']` opened." Its case `a UNION with rowActions: update: false does not survive rowActions: [edit]` asserted `{ trigger: true, edit: true, delete: false }`.

That pin **had to go red**, and did. It was deliberately pinned so that any behaviour change would force a re-read — the card says so and the triage comment confirmed it as a record, ⛔ not an endorsement. It has been **re-pointed at the intersection**, not deleted and not made green by weakening it:

- fact 3 in the file's docblock now states the ceiling, and says in the file itself that this file pinned the opposite until the ruling landed, so the next reader cannot mistake the flip for drift;
- the union's own shape is **kept** as the case that goes red if the `||` ever comes back — same inputs, opposite expectation (`{ trigger: false, edit: false, delete: false }`: with nothing left to offer the row grows no kebab at all);
- **the control now does more work than before, not less.** That describe block went from 2 cases to 5: the unnamed-member case (which a ceiling implemented as `update !== false` would pass while quietly keeping `rowActions`' old power to open), a control proving `rowActions` with no `operations` block still gets the wired-callback default, and the not-implemented case below.

**`packages/plugin-grid/src/__tests__/rowCrudAffordances.test.ts`** — the unit pin. Its case `honors explicit rowActions (edit/delete strings) when callbacks exist` asserted the same union at the function boundary and also flipped. Replaced by two cases: the selection alone can no longer open, and an explicit `operations` member `false` beats the selection per member.

## ⚠️ Declared deviation — half the ruling's formula is NOT implemented, on purpose

The ruling's expanded formula reads `canEdit = operationsUpdate AND (wantEditAction OR DEFAULT-WHEN-ROWACTIONS-ABSENT) AND hasOnEdit AND objectCanEdit`, and its prose adds that `rowActions` "chooses among what `operations` allows and can only narrow".

The **ceiling** half is implemented in full. The **narrowing** half is not, and could not be within this card's file surface:

- the gate cannot observe it. The call site collapses "`rowActions` absent" and "`rowActions` present without this name" into the same `false` (it passes `rowActionsList.includes('edit')`, and an absent `rowActions` becomes an empty array);
- narrowing on that `false` would close the generic Edit and Delete on **every** grid that declares no `rowActions` at all — the precise outcome the same ruling forbids one sentence earlier, "`operations` absent ⇒ today's defaults";
- so the only value of the ruling's `DEFAULT-WHEN-ROWACTIONS-ABSENT` hole that preserves the ruling's own stated invariant at this call site is "true", which collapses that conjunct away. That is what landed;
- telling the two apart needs a caller-side signal only `packages/plugin-grid/src/ObjectGrid.tsx` can produce — and that file is objectui#9837's surface, deliberately kept out of this batch. Per the dispatch I did not widen into it.

⭐ The gap is **pinned rather than left silent**: a case named `NOT IMPLEMENTED — rowActions does not NARROW inside the ceiling` records today's answer for `operations: { update: true, delete: true }` plus `rowActions: ['edit']`. Implementing the narrowing turns that case red, which is the re-read it should force. The same reasoning is written into the module docblock under "`operations` is the ceiling", so the next reader finds it at the code rather than in this description.

Recommended follow-up, ⛔ not filed by me: a card for the narrowing half, whose surface is the grid call site plus this gate's signature.

## Also NOT done, and why

- **The `describe` texts.** The ruling asks the `operations` and `rowActions` descriptions to state 「`operations` is the ceiling」. Those live in `packages/types/src/zod/objectql.zod.ts` (`operations` carries `Enabled operations`; `rowActions` carries no description at all), outside this card's declared file surface and in another package. Nothing published becomes false without it — neither description asserted the union — so this is a documentation gap, not a behaviour gap. The rule itself is stated in the module docblock here.
- **Docs.** `content/docs/plugins/plugin-grid.mdx`, `packages/plugin-grid/README.md` and `content/docs/api/schema-reference.md` mention both keys but neither asserts the union, so no published sentence is falsified by this change.

The **0** above is from the re-run after `pnpm --workspace-concurrency=2 --filter '@object-ui/plugin-grid^...' build` (exit 0). Both readings are reported rather than only the green one.

The test runs are repo-root invocations with repository-relative paths and no `--`, and each printed `RUN v4.1.10 /home/user/objectui-issue-9819` — the root, not a package directory. File counts are asserted, not assumed: 145 and 16, never a silent zero-match.

### ESLint — a declared narrowing, with the reading that makes it a measurement

The repository-wide `eslint . --no-inline-config` sweep is CI's run, never one this branch owes. What ran here is a targeted lint of the three changed source files, and the narrowing is proven rather than asserted:

1. **Population, read from ESLint's own config and not guessed** — `eslint.config.js` declares its blocks over `**/*.{ts,tsx}` with a top-level `ignores`; every block that could reach this branch's files is a path-glob block.
2. **File count, read from `--format json`** — 3 files linted, 0 errors, 2 warnings. Both warnings are `@typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any` and both are **pre-existing**: the same two, at shifted lines, on the base revision of the same file (measured by linting the base blob). This branch adds zero findings.
3. **Invariance over untouched files** — `eslint.config.js` declares **no** type-aware linting: no `parserOptions.project`, no `projectService`, no `tsconfigRootDir`, no `recommended-type-checked` preset. Every rule therefore judges one file from that file's own text, so no edit in this diff can move the verdict on any file this diff does not touch.

All three hold, so this is a measured narrowing rather than a check that simply did not run. Measured at head `3e7993e6`.

### Reverse verification (ablation)

Direction predicted **before** running: the re-pointed pins go red. That is what happened.

The fix was committed first, then the intersection was replaced on disk by the original union — anchor asserted to hit exactly once, and the substitution verified on disk in both directions (injected union present `1`, intersection absent `0`) rather than trusted from an editor's exit code.

- **mutation leg** — exit **1**: `Tests 4 failed | 51 passed (55)`. The four are exactly the ceiling assertions, and they span both pins and both projects: `|unit|` the two in `rowCrudAffordances.test.ts`, `|dom|` `the CEILING refuses: update: false SURVIVES rowActions: [edit]` and `the ceiling refuses a member the block does not NAME`. The control cases and the not-implemented case stayed green in both worlds, as they must.
- **restore leg** — `git checkout HEAD -- THE-PATH` (never the bare form, which would take the mutation back out of a polluted index), and the restore is proven by **bytes**, not by an exit code: `git hash-object` on disk equals the HEAD blob `c37fbbe437a10b567b0217d6957e010d0c7545fa`, and `git diff HEAD` is empty. Re-run: exit **0**, 55 passed.

Nothing from the ablation remains in the tree; the working tree is clean at `3e7993e6`.

## Acceptance notes

- Noted, not filed: `ObjectGrid.tsx`'s `hasRowActions` still counts `wantEditAction` / `wantDeleteAction` when deciding whether to render the actions COLUMN, so a view with `operations: { update: false }` plus `rowActions: ['edit']` renders an empty `_actions` cell instead of no column. Observable only as an empty right-hand cell — the kebab itself correctly does not appear (the menu plan's own empty guard). Carrier: objectui#9837's seat is the next one in that file. Not filed, and ⛔ not repaired here: the file is out of surface and the shape is the pre-existing "a row with nothing to offer renders an empty cell" behaviour, which that file documents deliberately.
- Noted, not filed: `rowCrudEffectiveOps.test.tsx` and `rowOperationsPerRow-8674.test.tsx` cover the layers ANDed on top of this gate and were unaffected — recorded so a later reader does not re-derive the blast radius from scratch. Carrier: none.

Re-checked independently: all 9 open pull requests were listed and their file lists read; none touches `packages/plugin-grid/src/`. The only plugin-grid overlap anywhere is objectui#8941, on `packages/plugin-grid/package.json` alone, which this branch does not touch.
